title: Nadir Shah Hears Why the Khalsa Cannot Be Broken

blocks.text: Nadir Shah asks Khan Bahadur who these Sikhs are after hearing repeated reports of their resistance. The answer begins with admiration: the Khalsa endure hunger and hardship, go without comfort in heat and cold, and still keep fighting with the energy of people sustained by conviction rather than provisions.

The page then sharpens that praise into martial proportion. The poem insists that each Singh fights a hundred, not because of numbers or equipment, but because death has lost its power to frighten those who see struggle for the faith as honorable.

Khan Bahadur traces their origin back to Guru Nanak and admits that Mughal injustice against the Gurus has brought its own punishment. Nadir Shah therefore concludes that those under God’s protection cannot truly be conquered by worldly rulers.
